name: Parchment
description:
A prepared sheet of pale animal skin, scraped smooth on both sides and cut to roughly 8 by 12 inches. It accepts ink well and can be rolled for storage.

The purchase is one blank sheet, not a scroll of magic. Ink, a pen and any preparation required for spell transcription or scroll crafting are separate; this sheet alone grants no such capability.

weight.notes: Two hundredths of a pound per dry sheet; bundles retain the sum of their individual weights.

source.title: Devil's Table: Goods & Provisions

name: Paper
description:
A single sheet of cream-coloured rag paper, roughly 8 by 12 inches, suitable for a letter, sketch or page of notes. Its faintly uneven edges show the marks of hand production.

Sold blank and unbound. Paper is easily spoiled by rain or a leaking flask; a protective case, writing implements and ink are separate purchases.

weight.notes: One hundredth of a pound per dry sheet, so a large stack still contributes to encumbrance.

name: Ink
description:
A small stoppered bottle of dark writing ink, holding 1 US fluid ounce. A few drops provide for ordinary notes or correspondence; the amount used depends on the writing surface and hand.

The listed weight includes the ink and bottle. Track partial use manually. Use 'Mark one ink bottle empty' only when the entire bottle has been spent; it removes one complete purchase from inventory. An empty bottle retained afterward must be recorded separately. This is ordinary ink, without magical or forgery benefits.
saleUnit: One stoppered bottle containing 1 US fluid ounce of ink

weight.notes: One tenth of a pound for the filled small bottle, including roughly 0.065 lb of ink and its lightweight vessel.

source.title: Devil's Table: Goods & Provisions

name: Ink Pen
description:
A sturdy quill trimmed to a fine nib for writing with bottled ink. It is a simple everyday implement for letters, accounts and travel notes.

Ink and a writing surface are not included. The nib may need occasional trimming with a suitable small blade. The pen grants no special ability to copy handwriting or create magical writings.

weight.notes: One hundredth of a pound for a single cut quill, keeping bulk purchases visible to encumbrance.

name: Chalk
description:
A short stick of soft white chalk for marking stone, timber or a reusable writing board. It is useful for tally marks, directions and temporary labels.

Chalk marks can rub away or wash off and are not reliable permanent trail signs. Track wear manually; no fixed number of marks or automatic trail-finding bonus is attached to the item.

weight.notes: Two hundredths of a pound for one small chalk stick.

name: Wax
description:
A small red bar of sealing wax for closing folded letters or impressing a simple seal. Gentle heat softens the end so a little wax can be dripped onto the chosen surface.

A bar is usually enough for about ten modest seals, depending on their size; track actual use manually. A heat source and stamp are separate. This wax is not a candle and does not establish the authenticity of a letter by itself.
saleUnit: One small bar of sealing wax

weight.notes: One twentieth of a pound for the small wax bar; the approximate seal count is a project guideline.

source.title: Devil's Table: Goods & Provisions

name: Sealing Stamp
description:
A small brass seal face mounted on a wooden handle. Its plain geometric mark leaves a clear impression in softened sealing wax.

The listed price covers a common stock design. Personal engraving, copied heraldry and official insignia require separate arrangements with a craftsperson. The stamp includes no wax and grants no automatic success at impersonation or forgery.
saleUnit: One brass-faced stamp with a simple geometric mark

weight.notes: One fifth of a pound for the brass face and short wooden handle.

source.title: Devil's Table: Goods & Provisions

name: Blank Book
description:
Forty blank paper leaves are stitched into a plain board-backed book, giving eighty writing faces. A cloth covering protects the spine and a cord closes the covers during travel.

Ink and pens are separate. This is ordinary stationery, without prepared spells, special ink or the fittings of a wizard's spellbook.
saleUnit: One bound book containing forty blank paper leaves

weight.notes: One and a quarter pounds for forty paper leaves, boards, binding and cover.

name: Ledger
description:
Twenty paper leaves are ruled into columns for dates, goods, quantities and sums. A firm cover supports writing at a counter and keeps loose edges together.

The book starts empty. Prices, debts and calculations must be recorded by its owner; it supplies neither an automatic account nor proof that a written transaction occurred.
saleUnit: One ruled account book containing twenty paper leaves

weight.notes: Three quarters of a pound for twenty ruled leaves and the protective binding.

name: Wax Tablet
description:
Two shallow wooden panels hold smooth wax writing surfaces and fold face-to-face for carrying. The included wooden stylus marks the wax; its broad end smooths out notes for reuse.

Heat can soften the wax and pressure can damage the writing. This temporary surface is not a sealed document, permanent archive or magical writing device.
saleUnit: One folding wax tablet with wooden stylus

weight.notes: Half a pound for both wax-filled panels, hinges and included stylus.

name: Slate
description:
A thin dark slate in a wooden frame takes chalk marks for tallies, lessons or messages. One ordinary chalk stick is supplied with it.

Wipe the face clean to reuse it. Rain, rubbing and hard knocks can destroy the writing; it is not intended as a durable travel map or legal record.
saleUnit: One framed writing slate with one chalk stick

weight.notes: One pound for the slate, wooden frame and included chalk stick.

name: Blotting Sand
description:
Fine dry sand dusted across fresh ink helps take up surface moisture before a sheet is handled. Shake off the surplus carefully once the ink has settled.

The packet includes its light wrapping. Sand does not remove an established mark or preserve ink against later soaking; manage its gradual use manually.
saleUnit: One quarter-pound packet of fine dry blotting sand

weight.notes: A quarter-pound packet of fine sand; its thin paper wrapper is included.

name: Document Case
description:
A stiff leather tube with a tied cap protects rolled sheets from ordinary crushing and handling. It holds up to ten rolled paper sheets or five thicker parchment sheets, subject to their actual size.

The case is sold empty. Its cap sheds a splash but is not an immersion seal; the stated paper count does not bypass the tube's physical fit.
saleUnit: One empty leather tube for rolled documents

weight.notes: Half a pound for the empty tube, cap and tie; documents are weighed separately.

source.title: Devil's Table: Goods & Provisions
